role.altitude: The credit counselor keeps explaining, interviewing, judging which debts come first and agreeing that with the client; chasing payslips, typing intake data and creditor claims, filing letters, booking payments and comparing debts by hand shrink.
skills_to_grow: Working from consented data and client uploads
role.ambitious_version: A counselor who has a client's full financial picture before the first meeting and uses the meeting for the person.

tasks.short: Look up the rules that apply to the client, explain general financial topics such as credit ratings, bankruptcy laws, consumer protection, wage attachments or collection actions, and check the client understood.

steps.what: Credit counselor looks up the rules that apply: protected income, wage attachment limits, collection steps
Credit counselor explains general financial topics to clients: credit report ratings, bankruptcy laws, wage attachments and collection actions
Credit counselor checks the client understood and answers questions in the session

tasks.design: The service keeps short, checked rule pages per topic, such as protected income, wage attachment limits and collection steps, with the current amounts, so the counselor looks them up in one place instead of searching laws and circulars. Explaining and checking understanding stay fully personal. Answering later questions and handing out materials are sibling tasks and are not priced here.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rules and amounts changed often and sat in many places.
tasks.enabler_now: Maintained rule pages with current amounts.
tasks.still_hard: Clients too stressed to take in information.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining a wage attachment so the client feels less afraid.

reach.learn: Whether shared rule pages reduce conflicting advice.

evidence.claim: A maintained page set with current amounts replaces searching laws and circulars.

assumptions: Boundary: explaining topics in the session; later questions (task 18933) and recommending materials (task 18944) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s1: a senior counselor keeps the rule pages current after each change in amounts or law.
Explaining and checking keep their full time.
research_questions: Do counselors give fewer outdated amounts?

incremental.description: Credit counselor keeps the rule pages current in turn with colleagues.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: experienced counselors who rarely look things up; high: new counselors and frequent rule changes.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Have the client fill in the intake form, collect income and tax documents, and interview clients by telephone or in person to gather financial information.

steps.what: Client fills in the online intake form with income, debts and expenses and uploads letters
Credit counselor collects payslips, benefit letters and tax data
Credit counselor interviews clients by telephone or in person to gather financial information not on paper

tasks.design: Before the first meeting the client fills in an online intake form and uploads creditor letters. With the client's consent, income, benefit and tax data come through a consented data-sharing service instead of the counselor chasing payslips and letters. Because routine facts such as household and income sources are already on the form, the interview spends less time on them and more on debts not on paper and what lies behind them. Entering the data in the file belongs to the records task and is priced there.
tasks.previous_blocker: Clients brought incomplete paperwork, and documents were chased over weeks.
tasks.enabler_now: Online intake forms and consented data-sharing from government sources.
tasks.still_hard: Debts the client is ashamed of or has forgotten.
tasks.human_edge: Asking the question that brings out the hidden debt.

reach.learn: Whether clients find the form manageable.

evidence.claim: A data-sharing service passes consented tax, benefits agency and government portal data to a lender, as an integration without a model.

assumptions: Boundary: gathering information; assessing the situation (task 18934) and recording it (task 18940) are sibling tasks.

Input contract for s2: income, benefit and tax data through the consented data-sharing service, for about 70% of clients who can log in and consent; the rest bring documents; s2 is priced at that share.
Clients' time on the form is shown in s1; it replaces part of what they told the counselor in the interview.
The interview keeps most of its time; only routine facts move to the form.
unknowns: Share of clients able to use the online form.
research_questions: Is the time from first contact to a complete picture shorter?

incremental.description: Credit counselor helps clients who get stuck on the form or the consent.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: clients who cannot use the form or consent; high: 70% of clients using both.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Write counseling session notes, file document images and creditor letters, enter intake data and creditor claims, record payments, record correspondence and client inquiries, and check the file before plan reviews.

steps.what: Credit counselor writes counseling session notes in the client file
Credit counselor scans and files client documents and creditor letters as document images
Credit counselor enters intake data and creditor claims into the client file
Credit counselor records financial transactions: payments received and paid out on client accounts
Credit counselor records correspondence and client inquiries in the file
Credit counselor checks the file for completeness before the plan review

tasks.design: Session notes use a template with fixed headings and pick lists for agreements. Documents and creditor letters arrive as client uploads with a document type chosen, so the counselor checks rather than scans. Intake answers and consented income data fill the client file, and the counselor checks them and adds creditor claims. Bank statements of client accounts are imported daily and matched to expected payments by rule, and the counselor handles only mismatches. Mail in the case mailbox is linked to the client file. Checking the file stays with the counselor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paper documents, retyped intake data and payments booked from statements by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Client portals, consented data-sharing, bank imports with matching rules and linked case mailboxes.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing that a new letter means a new problem.

ambition.what: See a missed payment the day after instead of at the monthly check.

tasks.altitude: Much less typing and filing; checking stays.

reach.learn: Whether payment problems are caught sooner.

evidence.claim: A data-sharing service passes consented tax, benefits agency and government portal data, as an integration without a model.
Bank feeds and rules over every record replace manual booking, with exceptions to a person.

assumptions: Boundary: keeping client records; disbursing funds (task 18951) and investigating payment problems (task 18954) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s2: client uploads through the portal, for about 70% of clients; the rest bring paper; s2 is priced at that share.
Input contract for s3: intake answers from the online form and consented income data from task 18939, for about 70% of clients; s3 is priced at that share.
Input contract for s4: daily statement import from the bank holding the client accounts; matching rules by amount and reference.
Checking the file keeps its full time.
unknowns: Share of payments that match automatically.
research_questions: Are files complete at plan reviews more often?

already_counted.description: Credit counselor resolves payments the matching rules cannot place.

incremental.description: Credit counselor keeps note templates, document types and matching rules current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mostly paper clients; high: 70% of clients using the portal and consent.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Build the comparison of debt costs and consequences, prioritize client debt repayment to avoid dire consequences or reduce costs, and agree the order with the client.

steps.what: Credit counselor builds the comparison of each debt: interest, arrears and the consequence of not paying
Credit counselor decides how to prioritize client debt repayment to avoid eviction, disconnection or foreclosure and reduce costs
Credit counselor discusses the order with the client and agrees it

tasks.design: From the creditor claims in the client file, a calculator lists each debt with its interest cost, arrears and a fixed rule flag for essential creditors such as rent, energy, health insurance and taxes, where not paying leads to eviction, disconnection or seizure, instead of the counselor building this in a spreadsheet. Deciding the order and agreeing it with the client stay with the counselor; no score decides for the client. Writing the order into the debt plan belongs to the plan task and is priced there.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each comparison was built by hand in a spreadsheet.
tasks.enabler_now: Calculators over the creditor claims in the client file.
tasks.still_hard: Creditors who will not wait whatever the order.
tasks.human_edge: Weighing a client's fear of one creditor against the cost of another.

reach.learn: Whether clients keep to the agreed order.

evidence.claim: A score is an automated decision when it is given a determining role; here the counselor decides.
Rules and arithmetic over loan data are plain code.

assumptions: Boundary: deciding the repayment order; writing the debt plan (task 18936) and negotiating with creditors (task 18941) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s1: creditor claims with amounts and interest entered in the client file under task 18940; essential creditor types kept as a fixed list by the service.
Deciding and agreeing keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of claims with known interest rates.
research_questions: Do fewer clients face eviction or disconnection during the plan?

incremental.description: Credit counselor checks the essential creditor list after rule changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few debts; high: many debts with different costs.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
